TWO BUILDS
==========

dist/preview-github-pages/   -> your preview link
dist/production/             -> the real domain, when it goes live

They are NOT interchangeable. The difference is the base path.


PREVIEW  (norvixhq.github.io/norvixco.com/)
-------------------------------------------
GitHub Pages project sites serve from a SUBPATH, so every root-absolute
path (/assets/site.css, /images/..., /logo/...) has been rewritten to
/norvixco.com/... — 44,959 references in total.

Also in this build, deliberately:
  · every page carries <meta name="robots" content="noindex, nofollow">
  · robots.txt is Disallow: /
  · no CNAME file
  · sitemap.xml points at the preview origin

That stops the preview being indexed and later competing with the real
site for the same content. Do not remove it while previewing.

To deploy: push the CONTENTS of dist/preview-github-pages/ to the repo
that serves norvixhq.github.io/norvixco.com/ (root of the repo, or the
/docs folder, depending on your Pages setting). .nojekyll is already
included, which Pages needs in order to serve the /assets folder.


PRODUCTION  (www.timberroofingandexteriors.com)
-----------------------------------------------
Root-absolute paths, indexable, CNAME included, sitemap on the real
domain. Upload the CONTENTS of dist/production/ to the web root.


REBUILDING
----------
  node build.js                                       production
  BASE_PATH=/norvixco.com PREVIEW=1 \
    PREVIEW_ORIGIN=https://norvixhq.github.io node build.js    preview

Change BASE_PATH if the repo name changes. A custom domain or a
user/org page (norvixhq.github.io with no subpath) needs no BASE_PATH
at all — build it as production.
